_metadata.description: Static mapping from ADMET-AI SDK Tox21 sub-assay output labels to matching Key Event (KE) and Molecular Initiating Event (MIE) IDs in the OECD AOP-Wiki bulk XML download (https://aopwiki.org/downloads).
_metadata.aop_wiki_source: OECD AOP Knowledge Base bulk XML download, aopwiki.org — Release 2.8 (March 2026)
notes: ADMET-AI outputs Tox21 sub-assay probabilities using short labels (e.g. 'NR-AhR'). These labels do not match any KE title verbatim in the AOP-Wiki XML.
This map provides the corresponding AOP-Wiki Key Event IDs and titles, plus the AOP IDs where each KE serves as the Molecular Initiating Event (MIE).
NR-* assays (Nuclear Receptor) are clean MIEs — they measure direct ligand-receptor molecular interactions.
SR-* assays (Stress Response) measure downstream pathway activation; their upstream MIEs are listed where applicable.
For NR-AR-LBD and NR-ER-LBD: these are technically the same MIE as NR-AR and NR-ER respectively, measured through a ligand-binding-domain construct rather than full-length receptor.
KE event page URL format: https://aopwiki.org/events/{ke_id}

mappings.assay_description: Tox21 Nuclear Receptor Androgen Receptor (full-length) agonist assay. Positive = activates (agonizes) the full-length androgen receptor.
mappings.biological_mechanism: Androgen receptor agonism — direct ligand-receptor interaction initiating androgen receptor signalling.

primary_ke_mapping.match_quality: High — NR-AR directly measures androgen receptor agonism, which is the defined molecular initiating event in multiple AOPs.

secondary_ke_mappings.match_quality: High — used as MIE for AR-dependent carcinogenesis AOPs.

Androgen receptor activation leading to prostate cancer

mappings.assay_description: Tox21 Nuclear Receptor Androgen Receptor Ligand Binding Domain agonist assay. Positive = binds to / activates the androgen receptor LBD.
mappings.biological_mechanism: Androgen receptor ligand binding domain agonism — same molecular initiating event as NR-AR, measured via a truncated LBD construct.

primary_ke_mapping.match_quality: High — the LBD assay measures the same MIE as NR-AR (androgen receptor agonism) through the ligand binding pocket.

mappings.notes: NR-AR-LBD is a variant assay format of NR-AR; both map to the same KE/MIE in AOP-Wiki. LBD assays are generally more specific to direct ligand binding vs. co-activator recruitment.

mappings.assay_description: Tox21 Nuclear Receptor Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor agonist assay. Positive = activates the AhR / aryl hydrocarbon receptor.
mappings.biological_mechanism: Aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR) activation — ligand binding leading to AhR-ARNT dimerisation and downstream CYP1A1 induction and other transcriptional changes.

primary_ke_mapping.match_quality: High — NR-AhR directly measures AhR activation, which is used as MIE in at least 14 AOPs.

mappings.assay_description: Tox21 Nuclear Receptor Aromatase inhibition assay. Positive = inhibits aromatase (CYP19A1), the enzyme that converts androgens to estrogens.
mappings.biological_mechanism: Aromatase (CYP19A1) enzyme inhibition — direct binding to and inhibition of the aromatase enzyme, reducing estrogen biosynthesis.

primary_ke_mapping.match_quality: High — NR-Aromatase positive calls indicate aromatase inhibition, which is the defined MIE in several AOPs. Note: this assay measures INHIBITORS, so positive = inhibitor.

secondary_ke_mappings.ke_title: reduction in ovarian granulosa cells, Aromatase (Cyp19a1)
secondary_ke_mappings.match_quality: Moderate — this KE is the MIE for AOP 7 (cell-level aromatase reduction rather than direct enzymatic inhibition).

mappings.notes: The Tox21 NR-Aromatase assay measures aromatase INHIBITORS. A positive result corresponds to 'Inhibition, Aromatase' (KE 36). The AOP-Wiki also includes AOPs for aromatase inhibition leading to: reproductive dysfunction in fish (AOP 25), male-biased sex ratio (AOP 346), impaired fecundity in female fish (AOP 289), and impaired fertility (AOP 271).

mappings.assay_description: Tox21 Nuclear Receptor Estrogen Receptor alpha (full-length) agonist assay. Positive = activates the full-length estrogen receptor alpha.
mappings.biological_mechanism: Estrogen receptor (ERα) agonism — direct ligand binding and activation of estrogen receptor alpha.

primary_ke_mapping.match_quality: High — NR-ER directly measures estrogen receptor agonism, which is the defined MIE in several reproductive toxicity AOPs.

secondary_ke_mappings.match_quality: High — used as MIE in several carcinogenesis and endocrine disruption AOPs.
High — used as MIE in AOP 200 (ER activation leading to breast cancer).
High — specific to ERα agonism, MIE in AOP 445 (ERα Agonism leads to Impaired Reproduction).

mappings.assay_description: Tox21 Nuclear Receptor Estrogen Receptor Ligand Binding Domain agonist assay. Positive = binds to / activates the estrogen receptor LBD.
mappings.biological_mechanism: Estrogen receptor alpha ligand binding domain agonism — same MIE as NR-ER, measured via truncated LBD construct.

primary_ke_mapping.match_quality: High — same MIE as NR-ER; LBD assay format measures the same ligand-binding molecular event.

mappings.notes: NR-ER-LBD is a variant assay format of NR-ER. Both map to the same KE/MIE in AOP-Wiki. LBD assays are generally more specific to direct ligand binding.

mappings.assay_description: Tox21 Nuclear Receptor PPAR-gamma (Peroxisome Proliferator-Activated Receptor gamma) agonist assay. Positive = activates PPAR-gamma.
mappings.biological_mechanism: Peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma (PPARγ) agonism — direct ligand binding and activation of PPARγ.

primary_ke_mapping.ke_title: Activation of specific nuclear receptors, PPAR-gamma activation
primary_ke_mapping.match_quality: High — NR-PPAR-gamma measures PPAR-gamma activation, which is the MIE in AOPs involving adipogenesis and sarcoma formation.

secondary_ke_mappings.ke_title: peroxisome proliferator activated receptor promoter demethylation
secondary_ke_mappings.match_quality: Low — epigenetic event upstream of PPAR-gamma activation; not the direct MIE measured by the NR-PPAR-gamma assay.

Epigenetic modification of PPARG leading to adipogenesis

mappings.assay_description: Tox21 Stress Response Antioxidant Response Element (ARE / Nrf2-ARE pathway) activation assay. Positive = activates the Nrf2/ARE oxidative stress pathway.
mappings.biological_mechanism: Nrf2/ARE pathway activation — electrophilic or oxidative stress triggers Nrf2 nuclear translocation and binding to antioxidant response elements, driving cytoprotective gene expression.
mappings.aop_wiki_mie_note: ARE/Nrf2 activation is NOT a primary MIE in AOP-Wiki; it is a downstream stress response KE. The upstream MIEs that cause ARE activation include oxidative stress-inducing chemicals (electrophiles, ROS generators, thiol-reactive agents).

primary_ke_mapping.match_quality: Moderate — SR-ARE measures Nrf2/ARE pathway activation; KE 478 represents Nrf2 activation as a downstream KE (typically in response to oxidative stress MIEs).

upstream_mie_ke_mappings.ke_title: Binding, Thiol/seleno-proteins involved in protection against oxidative stress
upstream_mie_ke_mappings.match_quality: Moderate — thiol reactivity is a common upstream MIE that activates ARE/Nrf2; used as MIE in AOP 17 and AOP 284.
Low — this is the opposite direction (repression) used as MIE in vascular disrupting effect AOPs.

mappings.notes: The SR-ARE assay is used in Tox21 as a general indicator of electrophilicity and oxidative stress induction. No single AOP-Wiki MIE maps cleanly because SR-ARE positivity can result from multiple upstream MIEs (electrophilic binding, ROS generation, etc.).

mappings.assay_description: Tox21 Stress Response ATAD5 genotoxicity assay. Positive = induces genotoxic/DNA-damaging stress (ATAD5 is upregulated in response to DNA replication stress and DNA damage).
mappings.biological_mechanism: DNA damage induction — ATAD5 (a DNA replication factor) is induced by genotoxic stress; SR-ATAD5 is used as a broad genotoxicity/DNA damage biomarker in Tox21.
mappings.aop_wiki_mie_note: ATAD5 itself is not defined as an MIE in AOP-Wiki. The assay detects broad DNA damage; multiple upstream MIEs can be responsible (alkylation, intercalation, strand breaks, etc.).

primary_ke_mapping.match_quality: Moderate — SR-ATAD5 positivity indicates DNA damage, which KE 1194 represents. However, this is typically a downstream KE, not the MIE.

upstream_mie_ke_mappings.match_quality: Moderate — DNA alkylation is a common upstream MIE leading to DNA damage detected by SR-ATAD5.
Moderate — bulky DNA adduct formation is an MIE in AOP 397 (Bulky DNA adducts leading to mutations).
Low — ionizing radiation MIE relevant to radiation-induced DNA damage contexts.

mappings.notes: SR-ATAD5 is a broad genotoxicity flag used in Tox21 risk profiling. There is no single AOP-Wiki MIE that cleanly maps to it. It is best interpreted as evidence of one of several DNA-damage MIEs (alkylation, intercalation, strand breakage, oxidative DNA damage).

mappings.assay_description: Tox21 Stress Response Heat Shock Element (HSE) activation assay. Positive = induces the heat shock response (HSF1 activation and HSP upregulation via heat shock elements).
mappings.biological_mechanism: Heat shock response / proteotoxic stress — protein denaturation or unfolded protein accumulation activates heat shock factor 1 (HSF1), driving HSP70/HSP90 expression via HSE motifs.
mappings.aop_wiki_mie_note: Heat shock element activation is not defined as an MIE in the AOP-Wiki. The pathway represents a cellular proteotoxic stress response; upstream MIEs include protein-reactive chemicals, mitochondrial toxicants, and general cytotoxins.

primary_ke_mapping.match_quality: Low-Moderate — the unfolded protein response (ER stress) and the heat shock response are distinct but related proteostasis pathways. SR-HSE positivity may co-occur with UPR activation.

upstream_mie_ke_mappings.match_quality: Low-Moderate — covalent protein modification can trigger heat shock response; used as MIE in AOP 38 (Protein Alkylation leading to Liver Fibrosis).
Low — oxidative protein damage can activate heat shock response.

mappings.notes: SR-HSE is a general proteotoxic stress indicator. No single AOP-Wiki MIE maps well to it. Chemicals that are positive in SR-HSE are often reactive species that damage or denature proteins. There is no dedicated 'Heat Shock Response' AOP in AOP-Wiki at time of writing.

representative_aops.aop_title: Protein Alkylation leading to Liver Fibrosis
Renal protein alkylation leading to kidney toxicity

mappings.assay_description: Tox21 Stress Response Mitochondrial Membrane Potential disruption assay. Positive = disrupts mitochondrial membrane potential (ΔΨm).
mappings.biological_mechanism: Mitochondrial membrane potential disruption — depolarization of the inner mitochondrial membrane, indicating mitochondrial toxicity (uncoupling, ETC inhibition, MPT pore opening).
mappings.aop_wiki_mie_note: Disruption of mitochondrial membrane potential is a downstream KE, not an MIE, in AOP-Wiki. Upstream MIEs that cause MMP disruption include inhibition of ETC complexes, uncouplers, and mitochondrial reactive compound binding.

primary_ke_mapping.match_quality: High for KE matching — SR-MMP directly measures this KE. However it is a downstream KE in AOP-Wiki, not an MIE.

secondary_ke_mappings.match_quality: Moderate — general mitochondrial dysfunction KE used across many AOPs.

upstream_mie_ke_mappings.ke_title: Inhibition, Mitochondrial Electron Transport Chain Complexes
upstream_mie_ke_mappings.match_quality: High — ETC inhibition is an upstream MIE that directly causes MMP disruption; used as MIE in AOPs 437, 447, 479, 480.

upstream_mie_ke_mappings.ke_title: Binding of inhibitor, NADH-ubiquinone oxidoreductase (complex I)
upstream_mie_ke_mappings.match_quality: High — Complex I binding is an MIE in AOP 3 (parkinsonian motor deficits) and AOP 273/276.
Moderate — uncoupling agents directly disrupt MMP; used as MIE-proximal KE in multiple AOPs.

mappings.notes: SR-MMP positive hits span multiple upstream MIE classes: ETC inhibitors (rotenone-like), uncouplers (FCCP-like), and redox-cycling agents. The best upstream MIE in AOP-Wiki for SR-MMP-positive chemicals is 'Inhibition, Mitochondrial Electron Transport Chain Complexes' (KE 105).

mappings.assay_description: Tox21 Stress Response p53 pathway activation assay. Positive = activates the p53 tumour suppressor pathway (DNA damage, replication stress, or other genotoxic events).
mappings.biological_mechanism: p53 pathway activation — stabilization and activation of TP53 in response to DNA strand breaks, nucleotide depletion, oxidative DNA damage, or replication stress.
mappings.aop_wiki_mie_note: p53 pathway activation is a downstream stress-response KE in AOP-Wiki, not an MIE. The upstream MIEs causing p53 activation include DNA alkylation, deposition of ionizing energy, bulky adduct formation, and other forms of genotoxicity.

primary_ke_mapping.match_quality: High for KE matching — SR-p53 directly measures this KE. However, it is a downstream KE in AOP-Wiki (used as KE in AOP 419 and AOP 441), not an MIE.

secondary_ke_mappings.ke_title: Altered gene expression, P53 dependent apoptosis pathway
secondary_ke_mappings.match_quality: Moderate — this KE represents downstream P53-dependent gene expression changes in AOP 419 (AhR activation leading to decreased lung function via P53 pathway).

upstream_mie_ke_mappings.match_quality: High — DNA alkylation is a primary MIE that activates p53 pathway; used as MIE in AOPs 15, 139, 322.
High — ionizing radiation MIE leading to DNA strand breaks and p53 activation; used as MIE in AOPs 272, 432, 441, 478, 482, 483.
Moderate — bulky adducts trigger NER and p53 activation; MIE in AOP 397.
Low-Moderate — AhR activation can lead to p53 pathway activation in specific AOPs (e.g., AOP 419: AhR decreasing lung function via P53 pathway).

mappings.notes: SR-p53 is a broad genotoxicity and DNA-damage indicator in Tox21. Like SR-ATAD5, there is no single AOP-Wiki MIE that maps to it uniquely. It is best interpreted as evidence of one of several DNA-damaging MIEs.
